notes.title: Game Details 4: True Pryzm Mode
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/12e31dca0d51a61493afe630c634df8fae0394a0.jpg[/img]

Players who have beaten the game with a rank of B and above will notice that True Pryzm mode becomes unlocked next to New Game. What does this mode do? In short, Normal (New Game) mode was merely the tutorial to get you familiarized with the game mechanics and True Pryzm is the REAL difficulty of the game.

Changes in this mode include:
[list]
[*]Lower starting clarity
[*]Aggressive enemies that deal more damage
[*]New enemy types
[*]Hints that show new paths are all turned off
[*]Certain enemies carry more innate clarity to absorb
[*]New areas that expand the lore and can lead to the true ending (hint is in the image)
[/list]
True Pryzm will test all that you've learnt from Normal mode and challenge the strategy that you will follow. There is more than one way to make it out and it is dependent on what you are trying to achieve. Are you merely trying to escape? Are you trying to save specific survivors? Are you aiming for the fastest completion time? Or are you going for the best rank of S? Whatever it is, give this mode a try when you're ready. Normal and True Pryzm have their own leaderboards. Can you get the best times in both?

Note: Continue+ works for True Pryzm as well, but there is only one Continue+ active at any time. So starting a New Game in Normal will wipe the one for True Pryzm and vice versa.

notes.title: Game Details 3: Continue+ Mode
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/c173c09027f9a03cf0fedaf1a3cae782a0a568ce.jpg[/img]

Have you survived the Przym or are you still trapped in it? Either way, you may have been wondering what the Continue+ option does.

Every new game changes certain parameters that requires a slightly different escape strategy. The overall story is generally the same, but how you survive it varies, especially if aiming for a good rank or specific achievements. Pryzm offers players some help if they find it too difficult. This is where Continue+ comes in.

[h3]For those wondering how saving works, this game will always auto-save at the start of every area or scene so players do not have to complete a run in one sitting. Simply quit the game and pick up where you left off.[/h3]

Continue+ mode only appears just after you complete an entire game or get a game over, replacing the regular Continue auto-save file. Selecting it puts you back into the game at the start of the second act while retaining every parameter from the previous game. So if you discovered a path that gave you a bonus item or a quicker way to avoid enemies previously, those paths are still the same in Continue+! This will allow you to better plan how to make it to the ending and possibly achieve a better rank. Hindsight is indeed 20/20. And you get an increase in starting clarity too, effectively making every Continue+ easier and easier.

Do note that any form of continuing disqualifies the run from the online leaderboard, but qualifies for all achievements not requiring a 1CC. Also, starting a New Game will make this option disappear. Why would you do this instead of using Continue+? Because many of the parameters of the game are actually set by your choices in the first act, so you may want to start a new game to re-arrange the parameters based on your goals.

notes.title: Game Details 1: What Is Pryzm?
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821111/b1fed7823e1e3a0bbebe4f2268d951d33c3af7be.jpg[/img]

Now that I am more familiar with how the Steam backend works after releasing [i][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2262880/Heli-Cats/]Heli-Cats[/url][/i], I can finally bring [i]Pryzm[/i] to the platform and utilize the various functions that allow me to realize the game's full potential.

[i]Pryzm[/i] started out as an experimental browser game. Coming from a comics background, the adventure / visual novel genre is the most appropriate continuation for my kinds of stories. However, I am an arcade gamer at heart and such games run counter to the length of what is considered a "full" visual novel (which are usually overly long to the point of being superfluously written to reach a large word count). [i]Pryzm[/i] is my attempt at condensing a full story-based game down to an arcade-like experience.

[h3]In essence, this is an adventure game that can be completed in a relatively short amount of time, but can be replayed over and over to get a better result, namely a better time and end rank.[/h3]
The preferable way to play is to perform a 1CC (one credit clear) like an arcade game. Every new run will randomize key parameters that will require the player to prioritize and adjust their escape strategy based on their goals. With enough runs, players should figure out the most optimal ways to get the best timings.

Players can also take their time with the story if they have no interest in getting the fastest clear times. The game has an auto-save that allows breaks in between. However, do note that there is only ONE auto-save, so save scumming has no benefit except to drain resources, and continuing disqualifies the run from the online leaderboards.

Thrown into the mix is an easy to learn turn-based combat system that hinges on a risk and reward system. Fight or flight becomes an important element that can result in crucial conservation or boosting of resources, or completely mess up a good run. Being arcade-like, game overs are always round the corner, so players must always weigh their decisions to avoid unrecoverable mistakes.

[h3]The Steam version of this game will feature many new upgrades to the original version such as new animations, revamped systems, expanded story elements, configurable controller support, achievements that guide players to learn the lore, and online speedrun leaderboards![/h3]

If any of the above interests you, please wishlist the game. More details will be posted in the future to help players understand the mechanics and special features. Thank you for considering my very non-mainstream / niche games!
